verdict: Microsoft closed its fiscal year with revenue up 18% to $76.4B as Azure grew 39%, and it kept $27.2B as profit.

segments.name: Productivity and Business Processes
segments.note: Microsoft 365 for businesses (commercial cloud +18%), LinkedIn (+9%) and Dynamics 365 (+23%) — the software businesses sell to companies.

segments.name: Intelligent Cloud
segments.note: Azure cloud computing and server products; Azure revenue grew 39% as AI demand kept building.

segments.name: More Personal Computing
segments.note: Windows licences, Xbox, Surface devices and search ads. Windows OEM and Devices revenue rose 3%, Xbox content and services 13%, and search ads 21% outside traffic costs.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building new products and AI; up 10% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The sales force and marketing; up 7% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back-office and legal costs; down 11% YoY.

otherDetail: A net expense of $1,707M, mostly net losses on investments Microsoft accounts for under the equity method, which held back GAAP profit.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Azure growth stayed hot
takeaways.text: Azure revenue grew 39% and Microsoft Cloud reached $46.7B, up 27%. Intelligent Cloud overall grew 26% to $29.9B.

takeaways.title: A record fiscal year
takeaways.text: Fiscal 2025 revenue was $281.7B, up 15%, and net income was $101.8B, up 16% — Microsoft's first year past $100B of profit.

takeaways.title: Cash returns continued
takeaways.text: Microsoft returned $9.4B to shareholders in dividends and share repurchases during the quarter.
